subtopics.title: Universal Gravitation & Inverse-Square Law
warrants: Newton's 3rd law action-reaction symmetry |F12| = |F21| holds strictly regardless of mass ratio.
Inverse-square radial law F = G*m1*m2/r^2 applies to point masses and spherical shells via shell theorem.
Zero external force implies internal gravity cannot displace the system center of mass.

subtopics.title: Surface Gravity & Planetary Scaling
warrants: Surface gravity g = G*M/R^2 = (4/3)*pi*G*rho*R connects density and radius scaling.
When mass scales as rho*R^3, simultaneous density and mass changes must account for radius contraction.

subtopics.title: Variation of g (Altitude vs. Depth)
warrants: Interior gravity scales linearly g(r) = g0*(r/R) due to cancellation of external concentric shell mass.
Exterior gravity falls off as inverse square g(r) = g0*(R/r)^2.
Shell theorem guarantees exact zero field inside any hollow uniform concentric cavity.

subtopics.title: Free Fall, Apparent Weight, & Weightlessness
warrants: Apparent weight is normal contact reaction N = m*(g ± a). True weight mg never vanishes in orbit.
Orbiting occupants and spacecraft share identical free-fall acceleration, producing contact weightlessness (N = 0).

subtopics.title: Kepler's Laws & Planetary Kinematics
warrants: Kepler 2nd law dA/dt = L/(2m) = constant is a direct consequence of central force torque tau = r x F = 0.
Kepler 3rd law T^2 / a^3 = 4*pi^2 / (G*M) holds for all closed Keplerian orbits with semimajor axis a.

subtopics.title: Satellite Dynamics & Energy Accounting
warrants: Circular orbital velocity v0 = sqrt(G*M/r) decreases with radius, but total energy E = -K = (1/2)*U increases (less negative).
Atmospheric drag removes total mechanical energy dE < 0, forcing orbital contraction dr < 0 and paradoxically increasing orbital speed (satellite paradox).

subtopics.title: Gravitational Potential & Escape Velocity
warrants: Zero potential reference is conventionally defined at infinity: U(r) = -G*M*m/r.
Escape speed v_e = sqrt(2*G*M/R) is completely independent of launch angle, provided trajectory clears the surface.
